name: annotation
comment: The Prism's judge of Web Annotations (app/src/PrismAnnotation.lex.tex over the table app/src/PrismAnnotationTable.lex.tex) held to the web-platform-tests annotation-model suite, the W3C Web Annotation Working Group's tests of the Web Annotation Data Model (Recommendation, 23 February 2017). A request is a test's name, a newline and the JSON-LD document submitted to it; the answer is ok, or the names of the test's assertions whose result is not the one the suite expects, in the test's order, or invalid for a test the suite does not have, for text that is not JSON (RFC 8259) and for an object that repeats a name (JSON-LD keeps names unique). 'suite' pins the revision and, by SHA-256, the seven tests, every assertion and definition schema the table is compiled from, and the suite's own runner and validator. 'content' pins every document the vectors submit: the suite's own samples, the Working Group's correct and incorrect examples (w3c/web-annotation), and the Recommendation's collection and page examples (its markup removed and its character references decoded). 'examples' are the acceptance vectors: each answer is what the suite's runner (scripts/JSONtest.js) reports with the suite's validator (scripts/ajv.min.js) for that document, so the guest is held to the suite's reading, including where the suite is stricter than the Recommendation (see app/specs/oracle/spec.json gaps). An assertion is claimed in the standards register only when these vectors show it both holding and failing.
